diagnostics.help: Adjust the state inline during render with a `prev`-prop comparison (`if (prop !== prevProp) { setPrevProp(prop); setX(...); }`), or refactor to remove the duplicated state. Routing the adjustment through a useEffect forces an extra render with a stale UI between the two commits. See https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect#adjusting-some-state-when-a-prop-changes

diagnostics.title: Multiple setState calls in one effect
diagnostics.message: 7 setState calls in one useEffect redraw your screen each time they run together.
diagnostics.help: Combine related updates in `useReducer` so one effect does not redraw the screen once per `setState` call.

diagnostics.title: React 19 API migration can break callers
diagnostics.message: useContext is replaced by `use()` in React 19, which reads context inside ifs & loops too, so switch to `import { use } from 'react'`.
diagnostics.help: Pass `ref` as a normal prop on function components, since `forwardRef` isn't needed in React 19. Replace `useContext(X)` with `use(X)`. Only runs on React 19+ projects.

diagnostics.title: Unstable context provider value
diagnostics.message: Every reader of this context redraws on each render because you build its `value` inline.
diagnostics.help: Wrap the context value in `useMemo` or move it outside the component so consumers do not redraw every render.

diagnostics.title: Pure function rebuilt every render
diagnostics.message: `handleWithdraw` inside `WalletPage` uses no local state but is rebuilt on every render, so it wastes work & breaks memoized children. Move it to the top of the file, outside the component.
diagnostics.help: Move the function above the component, at the top of the file. It doesn't use local state, so rebuilding it each update is wasted work.

diagnostics.title: Large inline style object rebuilds every render
diagnostics.message: This inline style has 10 properties, which is hard to read & rebuilds every render. Move it to a CSS class, CSS module, or styled component.
diagnostics.help: Move the styles to a CSS class, CSS module, Tailwind utilities, or a styled component. Big inline objects are hard to read and rebuild on every update.

diagnostics.title: Click handler missing keyboard handler
diagnostics.message: Keyboard users can't trigger this click handler because there's no keyboard one, so add `onKeyUp`, `onKeyDown`, or `onKeyPress`.
diagnostics.help: Pair `onClick` with a key handler so keyboard users can trigger it.

diagnostics.title: Interaction on static element
diagnostics.message: Screen reader users can't tell this click handler is interactive because it has no `role`, so add a `role` or use a button or link.
diagnostics.help: Give clickable static elements a `role`, or use a button or link.

diagnostics.title: Text is too small
diagnostics.message: Your users strain to read 11px text, so use at least 12px for body text, & 16px is best.
diagnostics.help: Use at least 12px for body text, and 16px is best. Small text is hard to read, especially on phones.

diagnostics.title: Effects chained together
diagnostics.message: Your screen redraws several times from a single action because one useEffect changes "orderId", which sets off this one.
diagnostics.help: Compute as much as possible during render (e.g. `const isGameOver = round > 5`) and write all related state inside the event handler that originally fires the chain. Each effect link adds an extra render and makes the code rigid as requirements evolve

diagnostics.title: Many related useState calls
diagnostics.message: 5 useState calls in "TrackingPage" can each trigger a separate render.
diagnostics.help: Group related state in `useReducer` so one logical update does not fan out into separate renders.

diagnostics.title: Event logic handled in an effect
diagnostics.message: Faking an event handler with state plus a useEffect costs an extra render & runs late.
diagnostics.help: Run the side effect in the event handler that triggers it, instead of watching its state from a useEffect. See https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect#sharing-logic-between-event-handlers

diagnostics.title: Button missing explicit type
diagnostics.message: Your users can submit the form by accident because a `<button>` with no `type` defaults to submit.
diagnostics.help: Set an explicit button `type` so plain buttons do not submit forms by accident: `type="button"`, `"submit"`, or `"reset"`.

diagnostics.title: State initialized from a mount effect
diagnostics.message: Your users see an extra render with empty "isOnline" because a useEffect sets its starting value.
diagnostics.help: Pass the initial value directly to useState() instead of setting it from a mount-only useEffect. For SSR hydration, prefer useSyncExternalStore().
